minutes.headline: Committee held off supporting the open space plan until school-property errors are fixed; approved Quebec trip.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed a draft open space plan, found errors in how school-owned land was listed and mapped, and had the chair ask the authors to correct them before any letter of support. It heard the eighth-grade Chromebook pilot report, a counselor's report on a conference about sexual misconduct prevention, and the superintendent's report on principal searches. It also approved a line-item transfer, minutes and the final Quebec trip.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to have the chair ask the open space plan's authors to correct errors about school-owned land, and no letter of support will be sent yet.
The committee indicated it wants to proceed on the understanding that the one-to-one Chromebook model continues next year, after hearing the eighth-grade pilot report.
The committee voted on a line-item transfer from the sewer dumping fees line to the fire safety line, for possible fire alarm troubleshooting costs at the middle high school.
The committee voted to give final approval for the Quebec field trip.

why_it_matters: A town land-use plan that lists or maps school property wrongly could shape how that land is treated later, so the committee's correction request bears on school sites.
Continuing the Chromebook model for a larger eighth-grade class draws on the technology budget, which residents will see in a later school budget.
